scope: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.8.1–.2 and §7.4.1–.5. Predictor parameters/algorithms §7.4.4.3–.4, CCITT/JBIG2, DCT/JPX, and crypt filters are excluded because prior shards own them.
primary_source_method: Effective ISO 32000-2 with EC3, checked against source text and footers; source pages noted below correspond to ISO printed pages (not the Markdown line mapping).

features.title: Stream object syntax, placement, and source
features.errata: No applicable EC3 correction found. Table 5 and §7.4.1 distinguish internal /Filter and external /FFilter.
features.ledger: Existing granular rows 7.3.8.1:syntax-and-object-placement, :stream-marker-eol, :length-and-delimiter, :post-endstream-whitespace, :external-file-source, :external-filter-parameters, :empty-stream, and :dl-is-hint (all ledger_status=implemented in doc/reviews/1983-specification-audit/features.json).
features.assertions: The external-source test uses paired exact-xref PDFs with and without /F; the ordinary control decodes its known payload while /F causes External at stream_source and no decoded stream. Example 3 asserts encoded extent and decoded bytes. Keyword-padding/extent tests assert EOL after stream and that an optional EOL before endstream is outside Length. Current source checks that /Length and endstream delimit a valid exact body; fallback search is explicitly recovery when the length cannot be followed/confirmed.
features.verdict: covered-at-the-inspected-features; no new external-file fetching obligation found
features.residuals: External stream data is intentionally unavailable to the reader: no host callback or filesystem open occurs. /FFilter and /FDecodeParms are accordingly not exercised. The producer requirements in Table 5 (stream indirect, dictionary required keys, no arbitrary excess bytes) do not by themselves require strict reader rejection of malformed files. I inspected the public refusal route and did not infer a missing fetch feature.

features.title: Length, encoded extent, EOD, and inferred data extent
features.errata: EC3 Issue #319 clarifies the encoded stream extent includes an enclosing filter EOD marker; Issue #527 corrects §7.4.1 Example 3's ASCII85 extent and /Length (447→449 after adding ~>).
features.ledger: Existing rows length-required-encoded-extent, eod-markers-are-encoded-data, self-limiting-filter-data, inferred-image-extent, inferred-sampled-function-extent, and no-extra-data (all represented under 7.3.8.2 in the feature inventory).
tests: crates/pdf-syntax/tests/serialize.rs (lying input length is recomputed on output)
features.assertions: Direct assertions cover a stated Length as encoded bytes, include ~> within encoded length, separate the permitted trailing EOL, and independently verify the corrected Example 3 decoded text. Stream-length-limit tests distinguish refusal at the resource bound from truncated/corrupt recovery. Image and sampled-function tests use their declared dimensions/size to assert short data is reported rather than fabricated as full sample content.
features.verdict: feature rows map to separate source-derived cases; no additional defect established
features.residuals: The clause's producer statement that all lengths, EOD markers, inferred lengths, and excess-data constraints be consistent is not a blanket command to refuse every malformed input. Current recovery paths are deliberately non-conforming-input policy. No dedicated assertion for arbitrary excess bytes was found, but an ISO reader rejection obligation was not established.

features.title: Filter selection, all Table 6 filters, order, and parameters
features.errata: EC3 Issue #527 corrects Example 3's literal data and length. No change to array order or /DecodeParms semantics.
features.assertions: The pipeline fixture starts with compressed bytes wrapped by ASCII85 and compares exact decoded bytes; corrected Example 3 is asserted separately. The Table 6 name test enumerates standard names and aliases and rejects an unsupported byte-filter route. DecodeParms tests discriminate array entry assignment/default handling. Predictor-specific internal rules are separately scoped out.
features.verdict: the inspected assertions support the ledger's main decoder promises
features.residuals: Table 6 includes image filters and Crypt, which have separate pipeline/image/encryption owners; this shard does not recertify them. The table's producer data-format requirements do not create rejection behavior for writer forms this application never emits.

features.title: ASCIIHex digit mapping, whitespace, end marker, odd nibble, and error report
features.errata: No erratum changes the pair mapping, EOD, odd-nibble padding, or error sentence.
features.ledger: Rows hex-pair-decoding, hex-whitespace, hex-eod, hex-foreign-character-error, and hex-odd-final-digit.
features.assertions: Mixed upper/lower digits separated by every §7.2 whitespace yield exact byte values; > stops before following bytes; odd final nibble is zero-padded; an illegal character is carried as ForeignCharacter while decoded prefix is retained. This is a recovery choice; the standard requires an error indication but does not prescribe refusal versus salvage.
features.verdict: confirmed for reviewed mapping and recovery assertions
features.residuals: Applying zero-padding at raw EOF with no > is extra recovery; not treated as a normative obligation.

features.title: ASCII85 grammar, groups, marker, numeric range, and windows
features.source_location: doc/md/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.md:1661–1679; source printed pp. 37–38; EC3 annotation for #98 at p. 53
features.errata: Issue #98 corrects the maximum 5-digit group to 2^32−1. Issue #293 adds: after `~`, the next character shall be `>` and any other character causes error. Issue #527 corrects Example 3.
features.assertions: For #293, valid z~> whole and pump controls yield four zeroes; z~x is Corrupt whole and Damage::Corrupt in the windowed path. Other tests assert canonical 1/2/3 byte final groups, z only between groups, legal upper bound versus uuuuu overflow, and the corrected Example 3 literal. These test the erratum rather than assume old pre-EC3 text.
features.verdict: marker erratum and inspected decoder branches are implemented; raw-EOF policy remains ambiguous by source
features.residuals: Whole-buffer ASCII85 treats a final `~` as successful end-of-input, while the pump marks the same unfinished two-byte marker Truncated. Source EC3 makes `~>` a two-byte marker, and code comments explicitly call the window case truncation; however §7.4.3 states producer encoding/error conditions, not a reader's exact recovery policy for a length-delimited truncated stream. ADR 0587 separates buffered structural consumers from windowed content consumers and accepts some damaged-data route distinctions. Candidate route-consistency test is drafted as an API/reporting-policy probe; do not call it an ISO-mandated reader rejection. The ledger appropriately marks no-marker EOF ambiguous.

features.title: LZW and Flate compression streams (predictor logic excluded)
features.errata: No applicable EC3 change identified in the method definitions; predictor notes/ranges are owned by a different shard.
features.ledger: Rows lzw-method-identification, flate-method-rfc1950-1951, compression-output-binary, lzw-code-space-and-meanings, initial-dictionary-and-synchronous-growth, maximum-table-entry, standard-lzw-example, lzw-msb-continuous-packing, lzw-eod-and-final-padding, clear-marker-restarts-decoder, full-table-clear-resets-width-and-dictionary; encoder-only steps/rules and compression ratio notes are correctly distinguished from reader requirements.
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/filter.rs:584–720 and Flate state near the Flate engine
features.assertions: Tests pin initial 9-bit packing, standard worked example, width transitions and reset/full-table clear, EOD, independent byte expectations, RFC zlib/raw Flate inputs, truncation/check-value reports, and resource bounds. Predictor assertions are explicitly excluded here.
features.verdict: granular decoder claims have direct assertion bodies; producer-only algorithm steps are not treated as reader obligations
features.residuals: This is a sampled audit, not a full rerun or certification of every LZW/Flate path. Existing test execution records in the repository are not execution evidence for this read-only turn. No tests run by this reviewer.

features.title: RunLength literal and repeated runs, EOD, extent, truncated recovery
tests: existing filter unit tests for incomplete literal/repeat runs
features.assertions: Boundary assertion independently derives literal length as header+1 and repeat length as 257−header at 0, 127, 129, and 255; EOD 128 closes the stream. Missing EOD retains `abc` with Damage::Truncated, which is local recovery rather than a normatively required reader response.
features.verdict: covered for inspected endpoints and recovery path
features.residuals: The stated NOTE compression ratios are informative only. No writer-side encoding duty arises for a reader-only filter crate.
